newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Striking Nigerian oil workers demand pay-off. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Striking Nigerian oil workers demand pay-off. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]

text.p: Staff of a contracting firm who have gone on a strike that has reduced Nigerian crude oil exports are demanding a pay-off because the company they work for has been sold off, their spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Port Harcourt in southeastern Nigeria that the dispute began after Ocean Inchcape Limited (O.I.L) of Britain was sold to U.S.-based Tidewater Inc.
"There are between 450-500 of us and some of us have been working for O.I.L. for more than 20 years," he said.
"We were demanding 10 years salary as pay-off but after long negotiation we have come down to one year but the management has not agreed to pay," he added.

The strike has forced Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit to declare force majeure on Bonny crude oil, which accounts for about half of its 950,000 barrels per day of crude oil output from Nigeria.

Shell says the delay of exports from Bonny light will be in effect for as long the strike lasts. O.I.L., a subsidiary of Ocean Group Plc, provides support services for tankers to berth and load crude oil.
(Corrects to clarify a delay of exports rather than a suspension).
The workers spokesman said the strike would be called off as soon as the local management of O.I.L. agreed to settle.
He claimed the London management of the company had phoned the staff on Tuesday to say the matter should be resolved peacefully.
"But up until now we have not seen our general manager," he said.
The general manager, a German whose name was given as Becker Jorge, was not available to comment.
